mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS indicates growing labor market strength, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Payroll employment growth does not translate into outperformance of SPX over the 20-day horizon in 70% of similar labor expansion episodes (rolling cross-section).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) followed by a rebound suggests a turning point in supply constraints, which can trigger a short-term demand surge that lifts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by 10% in the prior month then rises by 5% in the current month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX over the 5-day horizon when GDPC1 exhibits this pattern in other months (Granger causality test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above trend suggests improving supply chain conditions that reduce production costs and risks, supporting higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not coincide with SPX outperformance in 50% of similar upward trends (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in three months, it often coincides with a shift in monetary policy from tightening to holding, which can support equity valuations and produce positive 20-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in a 3-month window
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX when UNRATE crosses below 4% without a concurrent decline in 10-year yields (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 jobs signal a robust labor market, which can fuel wage growth and corporate investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days due to overvalued conditions.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX underperforms by at least 5% over the 60-day horizon in 80% of similar labor expansion episodes (backtest).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in housing starts (not available in the provided catalog, so this sketch is invalid - instead: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% suggests deflationary pressure that can reduce discount rates and support equity valuations, producing positive 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive SPX 20-day return when CPIAUCSL shows this pattern (robustness check across 5 inflation regimes).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (GDPC1) and unemployment (UNRATE) suggest a supply-demand balancing effect that reduces uncertainty and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX when GDPC1 and UNRATE move in opposite directions (Granger causality p < 0.05).
